name: Composite-geodesic resolution of the transport residual
claim: HYP-2026-006 is SUPPORTED with measured transport time T = 2.250 against predicted T_predicted = (pi/2)*l_AdS = 2.266 -- a 0.72% residual. This hypothesis claims the residual 0.72% (and its weak growth toward larger N: T*L = 36.0 at N=16 vs 37.2 at N=24) is NOT pure finite-size thread-discreteness noise but a SYSTEMATIC undercounting that arises from treating the bulk transport path as a purely spacelike geodesic. The correct object (Bohra-Sivaramakrishnan arXiv:2511.22168) is a single COMPOSITE timelike-then-spacelike worldline, which projects to ONE smooth geodesic in the dS2 kinematic space of AdS3. Specifically: the composite path's kinematic-space length L_dS2 is a single geodesic distance in dS2, and L_dS2 exactly reproduces T = (pi/2)*l_AdS with NO factor-of-2-style deficit, whereas the spacelike-only decomposition systematically undershoots by a calculable amount delta(N) that vanishes as 1/N. Quantitatively, the hypothesis predicts that re-expressing the existing transport theta-files as a dS2 kinematic-space geodesic length will (a) reduce the residual from 0.72% to below 0.2% at N=16, and (b) reproduce the observed N=16 -> N=24 trend as the predicted 1/N decay of delta(N) rather than as l_AdS-scaling noise.
confidence_rationale: Medium. (1) The kinematic-space framework is well-established and Bohra-Sivaramakrishnan 2511.22168 explicitly constructs the composite timelike-spacelike geodesic as a single dS2 curve -- this is a published, derivable object, not a conjectured form. (2) HYP-006's own experimental_evidence already records that the factor-of-2 discrepancy was resolved by the composite (null) geodesic formula T = (pi/2)*l_AdS (Bohra-Sivaramakrishnan, PAPER-2026-020), so the conceptual link is not speculative -- this hypothesis extends that resolution from the leading-order formula to the residual. (3) Held below high because the claim is specifically about the SIGN and FUNCTIONAL FORM of a sub-1% residual, which is close to the numerical noise floor of the existing theta-files; distinguishing a systematic 1/N delta from thread-discreteness 1/N noise (Lin 2026, PRL) requires the two N-points (16, 24) plus the dS2 recomputation, and two points is a weak basis for a 1/N fit. The test is zero-cost, so the weak basis is acceptable as a screening test.
test_design: Zero-cost re-analysis; NO new simulation or quantum circuit. Steps: (1) Load the existing transport theta-files for HYP-006 (research/data/simulations/holographic_transport.json, composite_geodesic_results.json, boundary_density_Y.npy / boundary_density_Z.npy) at N=16 and N=24. (2) From Bohra-Sivaramakrishnan 2511.22168, write the map from a composite (timelike segment + spacelike segment) bulk path to a single dS2 kinematic-space geodesic; the kinematic-space line element is the de Sitter metric ds^2_dS2 = (dalpha^2 - dbeta^2)/sin^2(...) over the (boundary-interval endpoint) coordinates. (3) For the measured transport event (peak at t=0.70, dip near-zero at t=2.50, reappearance at t=4.75 per HYP-006), compute the dS2 geodesic length L_dS2 connecting the source and reappearance boundary intervals. (4) Compare L_dS2 to T_measured = 2.250 and to the spacelike-only prediction. (5) Compute delta(N) = (spacelike prediction - composite prediction) at N=16 and N=24; test whether delta(N) follows 1/N and whether T_measured + delta(N) collapses the residual below 0.2%. Implementation: ~40-60 lines Python/NumPy reusing composite_geodesic_test.py infrastructure already in research/data/simulations/.
refutation_criteria: REFUTED if any hold: (a) the dS2 composite-geodesic length L_dS2 does NOT bring the N=16 residual below 0.2% (i.e. it is no better, or worse, than the existing spacelike (pi/2)*l_AdS prediction at 0.72%); (b) delta(N) computed at N=16 and N=24 has the WRONG SIGN (composite path predicts a LONGER transport time than spacelike, so the residual would grow rather than shrink) or does not decrease from N=16 to N=24; (c) the spacelike-only and composite dS2 predictions are numerically indistinguishable at the precision of the existing theta-files (residual difference < numerical noise), in which case the hypothesis is untestable on current data and must be marked NEEDS_REFINEMENT, not supported. Any of these means the 0.72% residual is NOT explained by spacelike-vs-composite geodesic choice and is more likely pure thread-discreteness (Lin 2026) finite-size noise.
hardware_required: Local CPU only. Python/NumPy re-analysis of existing HYP-006 transport theta-files in research/data/simulations/. No quantum hardware, no new simulation.
feasibility_notes: FEASIBILITY-CHECKER VERDICT (2026-05-15): OVERRIDE of the conjecture-generator's proposed TESTABLE_NOW. Correct verdict is NEEDS_REFINEMENT, because the hypothesis's own refutation criterion (c) ('untestable on current data -> NEEDS_REFINEMENT, not supported') is triggered A PRIORI by a hard data-resolution fact. (1) DATA AVAILABILITY: the referenced files exist for BOTH N=16 and N=24 (holographic_transport.json, composite_geodesic_results.json, boundary_density_{Y,Z}{,_24q}.npy, transport_times{,_24q}.npy, transport_max_rho{,_24q}.npy). composite_geodesic_test.py is reusable. So the test is computable in principle and zero-cost. (2) BLOCKING ISSUE -- RESOLUTION FLOOR (verified, not estimated): the residual this hypothesis exists to explain is 0.72% of T=2.250 = 0.0162 in absolute time units. The transport time is read off transport_times.npy / transport_times_24q.npy, which are BOTH a uniform grid of dt=0.05 over t in [0,6] (121 points; verified by direct load). The measured peak/dip/reappear times (0.70, 2.50, 4.75) are all exact multiples of 0.05 -- i.e. T_measured is GRID-QUANTIZED to +/-0.05 (+/-2.2% of T). The 0.0162 residual is 3.1x SMALLER than one time step. The hypothesis further predicts delta(N) brings the residual below 0.2% (~0.0045 abs) -- that is ~11x below the grid resolution. The dS2 composite-geodesic length L_dS2 is a closed-form analytic quantity (no resolution limit), but it must be COMPARED against the grid-quantized T_measured; that comparison cannot resolve a sub-step systematic from pure grid quantization. Therefore the spacelike-vs-composite difference is, on the current theta-files, BELOW the data's numerical/temporal precision -- exactly the condition the hypothesis itself defines as 'untestable on current data, mark NEEDS_REFINEMENT'. (3) Secondary issue: composite_geodesic_results.json stores only scalar summaries (T_measured, T_null, percent_error), not a theta-resolved geodesic integrand, so even the analytic side has no per-angle structure to fit a 1/N delta against beyond the two grid-locked N-points. WHAT WOULD UNBLOCK: re-run the HYP-006 transport time-evolution at dt <= 1e-3 (a >=50x finer grid; the holographic_transport_16q.py / _24q.py infrastructure already exists and a finer dt is a one-line change) for at least THREE N values (e.g. 12, 16, 24) so a systematic 1/N delta(N) can be separated from thread-discreteness 1/N noise with a non-degenerate fit. Estimated cost of that re-run: local statevector, 16-24q, a few hours total (same regime as the original HYP-006 runs, TESTABLE_NOW). Once a sub-0.2%-resolved transport curve exists at three N, this hypothesis becomes TESTABLE_NOW. Until then it is genuinely NEEDS_REFINEMENT -- not INFEASIBLE (no physics/math barrier; purely a data-resolution gap that a cheap re-run closes).
result_note_2026_05_16: SIM-2026-025 (2026-05-16): VERDICT REFUTED. Fine-dt re-run executed at dt=1e-3 for N=12 (25s, clean) and N=16 (13.7 min, clean). N=24 at dt=1e-3 is computationally infeasible (~7300 min projected; excluded). Key findings: (1) True N=16 residual at dt=1e-3 is -1.205% (T=2.2389), not the -0.72% (T=2.250) reported from the dt=0.05 grid -- the original figure was grid-quantization artifact, not the physics. (2) N=12 residual at dt=1e-3 is -2.777% (T=2.2033). (3) The O(1/N^2) Euler-Maclaurin/dS2 composite geodesic correction accounts for only 53% of the measured delta at N=16 -- criterion (a) fails: residual after dS2 correction is 0.562%, not below the 0.2% threshold. (4) The dominant finite-size correction is O(1/N), consistent with Lin (2026) thread-discreteness, not the O(1/N^2) composite dS2 geodesic. (5) delta(N) magnitude does decrease N=12->N=16 (direction correct), but the mechanism is thread-discreteness, not the dS2 geodesic. HYP-006 headline (T=(pi/2)*l_AdS SUPPORTED) is fully preserved -- this refutation only addresses the sub-1% residual's origin.
philosophical_implications: HYP-006 is one of the two SUPPORTED pillars of paper v4 (T = (pi/2)*l_AdS to 0.72%). This hypothesis does not threaten that pillar; it sharpens it. If the residual collapses under the composite dS2 geodesic, it would show that the worldline that information traverses in the emergent bulk is genuinely a single composite timelike-spacelike curve -- i.e. the boundary excitation does not merely take a spacelike shortcut, it propagates along a causal-then-acausal path that is ONE smooth object only in kinematic space. That elevates kinematic space from a calculational device to the natural arena in which holographic transport is geodesic, reinforcing the worldline interpretation at the heart of the project: propagation is proper-time-extremal, but the relevant proper time lives in dS2, not in the AdS bulk metric directly. It also models good Popperian hygiene: a SUPPORTED hypothesis still has a residual, and the disciplined move is to ask whether the residual is signal (composite geodesic) or noise (thread discreteness) via a zero-cost test with an explicit refutation gate.
